data.description:
The single highest-volume issue on c11's Sentry project. 941 events across 11 distinct users in one day (2026-07-25), all on release com.stage11.c11@0.58.0+116, environment production. Sentry issue C11-30, "main thread hang 2335ms".

STACK (from the hang watchdog's cross-thread capture; frames 0-21 of the wedged main thread):

  0  c11              MiddleClickCapture...
  1  SwiftUICore      _SizedShape
  2  SwiftUICore      ExclusiveGesture
  3  SwiftUICore      ExclusiveGesture
  4  c11              Foundation.URL? outlined copy
  5  c11              Bonsplit.TabBarView.horizontal...
  6  SwiftUI          ScrollViewReader.body
  7  SwiftUICore      DelayedPreferenceChild
  8  SwiftUICore      AttributeGraph.syncMainIfReferences
 ...
 17  AttributeGraph   AG::Graph::UpdateStack::update
 21  SwiftUICore      GraphHost.updatePreferences

READING. Main is inside a SwiftUI preference-key update pass (GraphHost.updatePreferences -> DelayedPreferenceChild -> syncMainIfReferences) driven from Bonsplit's TabBarView horizontal scroll body, with MiddleClickCapture and ExclusiveGesture in the evaluated subtree. `syncMainIfReferences` in an AttributeGraph update is the SwiftUI shape that blocks the main thread while resolving references; a 2.3s stall there means the tab bar's preference/ScrollViewReader machinery is re-evaluating a large subtree synchronously.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE STALL. CLAUDE.md already names TabItemView as a typing-latency hot path guarded by Equatable + .equatable() precisely so its body is not re-evaluated during typing. This stack is that guard failing (or being bypassed) at the container level: the cost is in TabBarView's own preference/gesture plumbing rather than in TabItemView's body. 11 of the operator base hit it in a single day.

WHERE TO LOOK.
  - vendor/bonsplit TabBarView horizontal scroll container: the ScrollViewReader + preference-key pair.
  - MiddleClickCapture's placement in that subtree — a gesture/NSViewRepresentable in a preference-writing branch forces re-evaluation.
  - The `Foundation.URL?` outlined copy at frame 4 suggests a URL-carrying value is being copied per tab per pass; a URL in a preference payload or Equatable key is worth ruling out.

ACCEPTANCE. A reproduction (many tabs + tab bar interaction) that stalls main >1s before the change and does not after; the Sentry issue does not recur on the next release with comparable install count. Note the outbound Sentry budget landed in #401, so recurrence now shows as fewer events, not zero: judge by issue presence and user count, not event count.

FOUND BY. Sentry audit 2026-08-04. Related: C11-186 (make main-thread hangs survivable) covers reporting/recovery for hangs in general; this ticket is one specific cause.
data.title: Main thread wedges ~2.3s in the tab bar's SwiftUI preference pass (941 Sentry events, 11 users)

data.body:
PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/403 (CI in the expected post-submodule-bump red; build-ghosttykit is running the checksum commit now)

**The ticket's reading of the stack is wrong, and I want that on the record before the fix.**
Sentry's payload is an on-device `backtrace_symbols()` dump resolved by nearest *exported*
symbol, which drifts badly across c11's non-exported Swift frames. The tell is in the quoted
stack itself: frame 4 `Foundation.URL? outlined copy` "calling" frame 3 `ExclusiveGesture`.
Outlined copy helpers are leaves. Those c11 frame names are noise; only the module column is
real.

The operator's own `~/Library/Logs/c11/hang.log` (151 MB, Jun 15 - Aug 4, 59 pids, 5001
episodes) carries the same records fully symbolicated. 9413 of 9433 futex-wedged captures are
`GhosttyNSView.attachSurface` <- `GhosttyTerminalView.updateNSView`, under the exact
`GraphHost.updatePreferences -> AttributeGraph` outer frames the ticket quotes. `TabBarView`
appears in 32 captures total.

**Root cause, disassembly-verified.** Every wedged sample is at `attachSurface + 372`, which in
the shipped binary is the return address of `bl reconcileAttachedWindowIfNeeded(for:)` (the next
call, `+388`, is `setKeyboardCopyModeActive`, and +388 frames appear in the same log). That
function's only blocking primitive is `ghostty_surface_set_display_id`, which pushes into the
renderer's bounded 64-slot mailbox with `.forever` -- no timeout -- and only notifies the
renderer *after* the push. Full queue + non-draining renderer = permanent main-thread deadlock.
Field instance: pid 6063, 2026-07-29, **13h58m wedged**, 9412 consecutive captures, no
`hang.end`. One deadlock episode is most of the event volume that made this the top issue.

The queue fills because `updateNSView` -> `attachSurface` re-pushed the display id on *every*
SwiftUI update, per terminal surface.

**Fix, two parts.**
1. c11: `GhosttyDisplayIDGate` in front of every call. The two per-update sites pass
   `force: false`; creation/focus/topology/screen-move sites keep `force: true`, because
   `renderer.setMacOSDisplayID` restarts a stalled CVDisplayLink on every message and that
   re-assert is how a stuck-vsync surface recovers.
2. ghostty fork (caf199071, 7604624d8): the export wakes the renderer first, pushes `.instant`,
   logs-and-drops when full. Generic, not c11-specific -- worth offering upstream.

**Measurement.**
- New Zig test: against a full queue the old call shape is still parked a full second later; the
  new one returns in <100ms. That is the >1s stall reproduced and removed at the swapped
  primitive.
- Tagged build (`reload.sh --tag c11-191`), driven session of 15 workspace-switch + typing rounds
  across 2 workspaces / 6 surfaces: **418 -> 30** renderer messages (13.9x). Cold launch:
  161 -> 30.
- Stated plainly in the PR: the local build links the prebuilt xcframework, so those counts
  measure the c11 half only, and I did not re-trigger the 14h app-level wedge end to end.

Note for C11-186: 7906 of 9433 wedged captures have main idle in `mach_msg2_trap` -- App
Nap / throttle false positives, not hangs. A large share of c11's hang telemetry is noise.

Trident plan review complete (9 reviewers + 4 syntheses). Verdict: FAIL plan-level (rework-then-rereview). Artifact art_01KZ77JYAR8Y1XEGK6J7SQ1XFP; full pack notes/trident-review-C11-191-plan-pack-20260804-1613/.

TRIAGE:
- Obvious (applied inline to plan): B2 lost-wakeup ordering corrected (push .instant then notify); I2 capture-vs-episode framing caveat added (9412/9423 captures = one 14h pid; ~0.2% of episodes); M1 upstream routing reworded (Stage-11-Agentics fork + operator flag, never manaflow-ai).
- Rework contract appended to plan for the author: B1 (unanimous 9/9 - delivery contract needed; drop-on-full + optimistic memo = permanently stale display link), B3-B7, I1 (focus/occlusion push .forever from main via same mailbox - fix the class or scope it out), I3-I6, M2-M3.
- Complex -> needs-human: S1 identification dispute (see needs-human flag).
- Skipping (evolutionary, out of scope this cycle): E1 embedding-safety contract as themed upstream contribution; E2 Sentry on-device fingerprinting fix; E3 hang-triage corpus script. Also surfaced-not-applied: S2 BlockingQueue signal->broadcast (single-waiter starvation is the 14h mechanism; termio can still starve post-fix), S3 bounded-push hotfix option, S4 PR split, S5 createSurface off-main dispute, S6 ~40% watchdog false-positive class (mach_msg2_trap captures -> C11-186), S7 hang.log 151MB unrotated (own ticket). These deserve tickets/answers but are not this plan's rework.

data.reason: S1: does this plan fix C11-191 at all? 4 reviewers say the Sentry hang (0.58.0+116, 941 events/11 users, bounded 2335ms, no libsystem_kernel leaf) is NOT the local attachSurface futex deadlock (0.60.1, 1 pid, 13h58m, __ulock_wait2 leaf) - the plan's own module-attribution rule contradicts its correction, and the ticket's TabBarView preference-storm signature exists locally symbolicated in ~32 episodes/10+ pids (candidate fix: vendor/bonsplit TabBarView.swift 730-749/794-809 unguarded onPreferenceChange->@State->frame(width:) loop). 2 reviewers accept the correction. Decisive sub-hour check: resolve one real 0.58.0+116 Sentry event frame-0 offset against that binary. Recommended: split - file the deadlock as its own P0 (real, disassembly-verified, force-quit-only) and keep C11-191 on the Sentry signature. Need your call on scope + acceptance criteria before plan rework resumes.

data.body:
**CI green on PR #403** — all 6 checks pass on a56f3d803 (build, build-ghosttykit, compat-tests,
remote-daemon-tests, web-typecheck, workflow-guard-tests). `build` runs c11LogicTests, so the new
`GhosttyDisplayIDGateTests` are covered there.

Two CI notes for whoever picks this up next:
- The ghostty bump produced the documented run-1 red (missing checksum pin), then
  `build-ghosttykit` pushed `a56f3d803`. Because that commit is authored by `github-actions[bot]`,
  its workflow runs land in `action_required` and sit there until approved — the CLAUDE.md
  writeup doesn't mention this step. Cleared with
  `gh api -X POST repos/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/actions/runs/<id>/approve`. Worth adding to the
  ghostty-bump section of CLAUDE.md.
- Unrelated papercut hit while instrumenting: `vendor/bonsplit` `DebugEventLog.resolveLogPath()`
  still reads only the legacy `CMUX_DEBUG_LOG` / `CMUX_TAG` / `CMUX_SOCKET_PATH` env vars, so
  `C11_DEBUG_LOG=... reload.sh --tag` silently writes to a bundle-id-derived path instead. Left
  alone here (submodule, out of scope), but it contradicts the repo's C11_* naming rule.

Left unmerged deliberately: the ticket's definition of done is an open PR with green CI, and this
touches a terminal-rendering hot path plus a submodule bump, so it wants a human look.

**Correction — the plan review is right and my attribution was wrong.**

I claimed Sentry C11-30 was the `attachSurface` futex deadlock. It probably is not. My argument
leaned on the `GraphHost.updatePreferences -> AttributeGraph` frames matching, but that is the
generic SwiftUI update spine and appears in *both* candidate signatures, so it discriminates
nothing. I also let a 9413-capture cluster stand in for episode frequency when it is a single
14-hour episode -- a number I had already computed and then failed to weigh.

Re-running the local log at episode level, the reviewers' read is better supported:

|                      | Sentry C11-30 | attachSurface deadlock | TabBarView signature |
|----------------------|---------------|------------------------|----------------------|
| distinct users/pids  | 11 users      | 5 pids, 6 episodes     | **11 pids**, 25 episodes, 14 days |
| duration             | ~2335 ms      | 14h, force-quit only   | median **2310 ms** |
| frame-0 module       | `c11` (userland) | `libsystem_kernel`  | userland (libswiftCore/SwiftUICore/AttributeGraph) |

11 pids vs 11 users and 2310 ms vs 2335 ms is a much better fit than one catastrophic wedge, and
the frame-0 module mismatch is decisive under my own stated rule (module attribution is reliable,
symbol names are not). The TabBarView captures show main genuinely burning CPU inside
`TabBarView.body` / `tabItem` / `contextMenuState` / `collapsedControlsRow` -- the ticket's
original reading.

**What I am NOT withdrawing:** the deadlock is real, disassembly-verified, force-quit-only, and
fixed with a timed regression test. PR #403 is green on all 6 checks. I have retitled and
rewritten it to stand on its own as a deadlock fix rather than as the fix for this ticket.

**Recommendation, matching the review:** split. #403 becomes its own P0. C11-191 stays on the
Sentry/tab-bar signature with the review's candidate as the lead (the unguarded
`onPreferenceChange` -> `@State` -> `.frame(width:)` cycle at bonsplit TabBarView.swift 730-749 /
794-809). I have the 25 local TabBarView episodes parsed and can hand them over.

Leaving NEEDS HUMAN in place and the status untouched -- the scope call is the operator's, and I
am not going to force a transition past a review gate I got wrong. Flagged in c11.

data.note: Operator call 2026-08-06: SPLIT. The deadlock is filed as C11-200 and its fix (#403) is merged as 8c7422b4f. C11-191 stays pointed at the Sentry tab-bar preference-pass signature (issue C11-30, still live and accumulating on 0.58.0+116). Plan rework resumes on that scope, starting from the candidate root cause the reviewers located: vendor/bonsplit TabBarView.swift 730-749/794-809, unguarded onPreferenceChange -> @State -> .frame(width:) feedback loop.

data.body:
**Plan rework, and the reviewers' candidate is not where the evidence points.**

I profiled all 32 local TabBarView captures / 25 episodes. Which TabBarView member is on the
stack: `horizontalBar` 43, `splitButtons` 23, `collapsedControlsRow` 5, `tabItem` 3. Nothing in
those stacks shows the `onPreferenceChange` -> `@State` -> `.frame(width:)` cycle spinning
(median max-repeat of any single frame is 5, and the repeats are AppKit `_layoutSubtreeWithOldSize`,
not the bonsplit preference keys). I do not think 730-749 / 794-809 is the cause. Happy to be
wrong, but I want to chase the stronger signal first.

**What the longest episode actually shows** (227,616 ms, pid 58841, 2026-07-30):

    35  c11         DefaultAgentConfigStore.current (getter)
    28-34 Foundation JSONDecoder.decode
    25  c11         DefaultAgentConfig.init(from:)     <- conformance thunk, reliable symbol
     8  c11         AgentConfig.init(from:)            <- conformance thunk, reliable symbol
     3-24 Foundation nested JSONDecoderImpl.KeyedContainer.decode
    39-44 SwiftUI    View.contextMenu(menuItems:) + ZStack   <- reliable (SwiftUI dylib)

A `DefaultAgentConfig` JSON decode running inside SwiftUI menu-content construction, on main.
`Sources/DefaultAgentConfig.swift:354` is a **computed property with no cache**: every access does
`UserDefaults.data(forKey:)` + a fresh `JSONDecoder().decode(...)` + a fill loop over
`AgentType.allCases`. Corroborating captures in the same log: one episode wedged in
`NSBundle _localizedStringForKey` under `AgentType.displayName`, and five captures blocked in
`-[NSUserDefaults objectForKey:]` -> `CFPrefsSource copyValueForKey` -> `__ulock_wait2`, i.e. this
path can block on the cfprefsd IPC lock, not merely burn CPU. That is exactly the shape of a
bounded multi-second stall that hits many users.

**Methodology correction I owe you:** I have been treating the *local* log's c11 frame names as
reliable. They are not -- same `backtrace_symbols`/dladdr nearest-exported-symbol mechanism as
Sentry. Proof: the 227s stack names `Workspace.splitTabBar(_:menuItemsForNewSurfaceKind:inPane:)`,
and `git log -S` across all history shows that method **never existed in this repo**. What is
trustworthy in these stacks is (a) the module column and (b) symbols from system dylibs with full
export tables -- which is why the Foundation/SwiftUI frames above carry the argument and the c11
frame names do not. The Swift `init(from:)` conformance thunks are the exception; those are
exported and they name `DefaultAgentConfig` outright.

**Proposed scope:** cache the decoded config in `DefaultAgentConfigStore` (invalidate on
`save`/`update` and on external UserDefaults change), and stop rebuilding agent menu content per
body pass. This is c11-side, no bonsplit submodule bump needed. I will not claim it closes C11-191
until I can tie it to a measured stall.

Branch: `c11-191-tabbar-preference-loop` off 643c64ca3 (will rename to match the real scope).

Re-staffed 2026-08-06. Previous agent was lost when c11 restarted. New agent launched on opus/high in the c11-191-tabbar-hang worktree (branch c11-191-tabbar-preference-loop) with the split decision, the bonsplit TabBarView candidate root cause, and the decisive frame-0 offset check as its brief.

**Refuted, with numbers. The bonsplit preference loop is 0.2% of the population, and Sentry C11-30 is not a signature at all.**

I did the check the reviewers proposed, then went past it: pulled 1,500 real events out of Sentry
C11-30 (group 7573742683) and re-parsed the operator's local `hang.log` (21,192 captures / 5,311
episodes / 63 pids, Jun 15 - Aug 6) with c11's own shipped classifier.

**1. C11-30 is a bucket, not a bug.** Its fingerprint is `{{ default }}`, one hash, and the 1,500
sampled events span **11 different release strings** (0.52.0 through 0.61.0, plus four debug
builds) and every stack shape there is. Sentry groups message events by the stack of the thread
that *reported* them, which for a hang report is always the watchdog's own loop, byte-identical
every time. `Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift` documents exactly this - it is the premise of
C11-192. So "941 events, 11 users, one issue" was never one cause, and no single root cause can
close it.

**2. The 2335 ms in the title is the detection threshold, not a signature.** At v0.58.0 there was
no Sentry-specific threshold: every episode was reported the moment the detector fired at
`stallThresholdMs = 2000`, and `gapMs` is the gap *at detection*. Median across the 1,231 sampled
0.58.0+116 events is 2334.5 ms because the distribution is truncated at 2 s, not because 2.3 s is
characteristic. Real episode length from the local `hang.end` records: median 6.7 s, p90 49 s, 16%
over 30 s, max 6.8 h.

**3. Sentry can't see our own frames.** `reportTelemetry` sends `stack.prefix(24)`. The SwiftUI
update spine is deeper than that, so **73% of busy 0.58.0+116 events carry zero c11 frames** - the
frames the ticket quotes ("MiddleClickCapture", "Bonsplit.TabBarView.horizontal...") are Sentry's
demangling of that generic spine, not evidence of a tab-bar culprit. This is a self-inflicted
evidence gap and it is cheap to close.

**4. Applying the shipped `MainThreadHangSignature` rules to all 5,311 local episodes** (i.e. what
the next release's Sentry will look like once C11-192 ships):

| bucket | episodes | share | pids |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runloop-idle` (main parked in `CFRunLoopServiceMachPort`) | 2470 | **46.5%** | 53 |
| `appkit` | 822 | 15.5% | 45 |
| `swiftui-update/hosting-begin-transaction` | 776 | 14.6% | 38 |
| `swiftui-update/hosting-layout` | 546 | 10.3% | 39 |
| `other` | 259 | 4.9% | 32 |
| `swiftui-update` (unphased) | 176 | 3.3% | 30 |
| `generic-metadata` | 131 | 2.5% | 28 |
| `lock-wait` | 76 | 1.4% | 16 |
| `xpc-sync-wait` | 42 | 0.8% | 17 |
| **`swiftui-update/preferences`** | **13** | **0.2%** | 7 |

Generously: `updatePreferences` appears anywhere in 190 episodes (3.6%); `TabBarView` anywhere in
25 (0.5%); **both together in 12 (0.23%)**. The ticket's candidate cause is the smallest bucket we
have.

**5. I also read the candidate code.** `TabBarView.swift` 730-749 / 794-809: the two preference
writers measure the trailing accessory and the split buttons; `onPreferenceChange` sets
`@State effectiveChromeWidth`, which feeds `.frame(width:)` on the *backdrop gradient sibling*
inside the same `ZStack`, not on the measured subtree. `resolvedEffectiveChromeWidth` reads
`effectiveChromeWidth` only in the zero-measurement fallback and returns it unchanged, so it is
idempotent. There is no divergent cycle, which is why no local capture ever shows those keys
spinning. Not a defect worth a submodule bump.

**Where that leaves the ticket.** The real user-visible freeze is `swiftui-update/*` (28.2%
combined, median 2.5-2.8 s at detection, no c11 frame on the stack in ~84% of them because of the
24-frame cut). The single largest slice of the top issue - 46.5% - is `runloop-idle`: main parked
in the run loop with a heartbeat that hasn't been drained. That is a delayed ack, not a wedged main
thread, and it is most of what made this the highest-volume issue.

Recommending the scope be re-pointed (asking the operator now): (a) stop reporting `runloop-idle`
as a hang when nobody was looking, and tag app-active/occluded state so the remainder is judgeable;
(b) send enough of the stack - top window plus the deepest own-module frames - that the SwiftUI
buckets become attributable in the field; then (c) a successor ticket chases
`swiftui-update/hosting-*` with evidence instead of a guess. All c11-side; no bonsplit bump.

Raw analysis scripts + harvested corpora kept out of the repo (session scratchpad).

**PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/411** (operator picked "fix the telemetry,
then chase", 2026-08-07). c11-side only, no bonsplit bump.

Two changes, both measured against the 5,311-episode local corpus:

1. **`runloop-idle` no longer reports from behind an unwatched window.** Main parked at the top of
   the run loop with the heartbeat undelivered is a late ack, not a wedge; off-screen that is App
   Nap and timer coalescing working as designed. 46.5% of all episodes, and the largest single
   slice of what made the aggregate hang issue c11's highest-volume report. Watched (frontmost +
   unoccluded) still reports, because then the UI died while someone was looking at it. The whole
   population still lands in the local hang log and in PostHog; only the outbound Sentry event is
   suppressed. Visibility is sampled on main from AppKit notifications into a lock-protected
   snapshot the watchdog reads while main is wedged.

2. **Reports carry the frames that name the workload.** `stack.prefix(24)` cut above our own
   frames: 73% of busy 0.58.0+116 events arrived with no c11 frame at all. `reportedStack` keeps
   the top window and appends the own-module frames from below it, true indices preserved and the
   elided run marked.

Plus `hang.app_active` / `hang.window_visible` tags, `cause=`/`active=`/`visible=` in the local log
header, and the same `cause` label on the PostHog event.

Tests are behavioral and live in `c11LogicTests`, so CI's `build` job runs them: the stack-window
selection (own frames from below, true indices, gap marker, no-op when it fits, bounded append)
and the reporting rule (unwatched idle suppressed, watched idle reported, every other cause
reported regardless).

**Successor filed: C11-202** — `swiftui-update/*` is 28.2% of episodes across 38-39 pids, median
2.5-2.8 s at detection, real episode median 6.7 s / p90 49 s. That is the freeze a human feels.
~84% of those captures name none of our code today, which is exactly what #411 fixes, so C11-202
starts by reading `hang.culprit` off the first release carrying #402 + #411 rather than guessing.
Its description carries the frame-0 distribution and the leading hypothesis (very large nested
generic view types in the sidebar/tab strip driving Swift-runtime metadata churn).

**Correction to my own number on #411, before it merges.**

I wrote that 73% of busy 0.58.0+116 Sentry events carry no c11 frame, and let that imply the
frame-window change recovers most of them. The first half is right; the implication is not, and I
should have measured it before claiming it.

Measured on the local corpus (2,241 busy episodes, full 96-frame captures):

| | busy episodes | share |
|---|---|---|
| own frame within the top 24 (already visible) | 404 | 18.0% |
| own frame only **below** 24 (what #411 recovers) | 68 | **3.0%** |
| no own frame anywhere in 96 frames | 1769 | 78.9% |

So the change lifts the share of busy reports that name our code from 18.0% to 21.0%. Real, cheap
(≤8 extra payload lines), and the difference between a nameless report and a full culprit chain —
but a 3-point lift, not a 73-point one. Only 165 of 5,311 captures hit the 96-frame cap, so the
missing frames are not hiding below it either: in ~79% of busy episodes main genuinely is inside
SwiftUI/AppKit internals with none of our code on the stack at any depth.

**Validation of the change itself** (executable, no `xcodebuild`: the shipped
`MainThreadHangSignature` spliced into a standalone harness, run over a real 96-frame capture from
the log — pid 17480, 2123 ms):

```
cause=swiftui-update phase=hosting-layout
OLD payload (prefix 24): own-module frames carried = 0
NEW payload: 32 lines
  23  AppKit  NSPerformVisuallyAtomicChange + 128
  …   65 frames elided
  51  c11  WindowTerminalPortal.synchronizeLayoutHierarchy + 52
  52  c11  WindowTerminalPortal.ensureInstalled + 1216
  53  c11  WindowTerminalPortal.synchronizeHostedView(withId:) + 60
  54  c11  WindowTerminalPortal.bind(hostedView:to:visibleInUI:zPriority:workspaceFrameStyle:) + 3380
  55  c11  TerminalWindowPortalRegistry.bind(...) + 784
  56  c11  GhosttyTerminalView.updateNSView(_:context:) + 652
  57  c11  GhosttyTerminalView.HostContainerView.viewDidMoveToWindow() + 100
```

That is exactly the class of report the change exists for: under the old payload this event named
nothing; under the new one it names the whole portal-bind chain under an `NSView
_layoutSubtreeWithOldSize:` pass.

**What this means for C11-202.** Its approach section says "wait for #411's data, then read
`hang.culprit`." That will help the ~21% of `swiftui-update` reports that name anything; for the
other 79% no amount of frames will, because our code is not on the stack. C11-202 needs a
profiler (Instruments SwiftUI + Time Profiler against a driven repro), not deeper post-hoc
sampling. Updating C11-202 to say so.

The `runloop-idle` half of #411 — the 46.5% — is unaffected by this correction.

**Merged: b2fb5caa5 (#411).** All 10 checks green (`build` runs the new `c11LogicTests` cases);
Drawbridge deep review verdict was "merge as-is, nothing blocking", having independently verified
the test-target membership, the lock discipline between main and the watchdog, and the narrowness
of the `runloop-idle` rule.

**What the ticket delivered.**
- The identification, settled with evidence rather than argument: Sentry C11-30 is a
  default-grouped bucket, not a signature; its "2335ms" is the 2s detection threshold; the
  tab-bar preference-loop candidate is 0.2% of episodes and the code path is idempotent.
- The largest slice of the volume (46.5%, `runloop-idle`) no longer reports from behind an
  unwatched window, because a late heartbeat ack is not a wedge.
- Reports that *can* name our code now do (18.0% -> 21.0% of busy reports), plus
  `hang.app_active` / `hang.window_visible` tags, `cause=`/`active=`/`visible=` in the local log
  header, and a matching `cause` on the PostHog event.

**Not done, and deliberately so.** No tagged-build smoke launch: the repo's standing instruction
defers local `xcodebuild` to CI, and this change's only user-visible surface is a Sentry payload.
The closest available real-artifact check was run instead — the shipped `MainThreadHangSignature`
spliced into a standalone harness and executed over a real 96-frame production capture (recorded
in the correction comment above). If a tagged validation gate is wanted before this ships in a
release, it is a small follow-up.

**Verification once it ships.** On the first release carrying #402 + #411, C11-30 should stop
accumulating and split into per-cause issues; `runloop-idle` should be a small fraction of its
former self, and the `swiftui-update/*` issues should start carrying `hang.culprit`. That is the
recurrence check this ticket's acceptance asked for, in the honest form: judge by issue presence
and user count per bucket, not by total event count.

Successor: **C11-202** (`swiftui-update/*`, 28.2% of episodes, the freeze a human actually feels),
with the culprit ranking, the worked portal-bind example, and the corrected approach (profiler
against a driven repro, because ~79% of those episodes name none of our code at any stack depth).

provenance.reason: Identification settled; telemetry fix merged as b2fb5caa5 (#411). Remaining work is C11-202.

data.body:
